
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Background Information</strong></p>

This project examines how land ownership patterns in Minnesota have changed over time using parcel-level data from the Minnesota Geospatial Information Office. Our primary goal is to analyze the rate at which land parcels transfer from one owner to another and to identify trends in ownership among individuals, corporations, and government entities. By studying these changes, we aim to better understand how land ownership influences economic development, land use, taxation, and environmental management across the state.

The dataset includes detailed information on parcel size, ownership, location, district, land type, assessed value, and property taxes. We are also working to incorporate a year variable so that ownership changes can be tracked over time. Using R, web scraping techniques, and geospatial visualization tools such as Quarto and Leaflet, we create interactive maps and charts that allow users to explore land ownership patterns throughout Minnesota. This project was developed as part of a data science course at St. Olaf College and demonstrates how data science can be used to answer important questions about land ownership and resource management.
